title: Why Big Companies Are Thinking Like Startups
summary: Large corporations like JPMorgan Chase are adopting startup methodologies to foster innovation and maintain competitiveness in a rapidly changing market. This involves minimizing waste, maximizing customer value, embracing Agile development, and implementing a "three horizons" framework for innovation, with a focus on continuous customer feedback. These strategies aim to accelerate product development and deliver value faster, much like their smaller, more nimble counterparts.

title: Groceries And Gadgets: The Robots Coming To A Supermarket Near You
summary: This article discusses the increasing presence of robots in supermarkets like Walmart and Stop & Shop, used for tasks such as inventory monitoring, cleaning spills, and unloading trucks. The implementation of these robots raises questions about their impact on labor, with companies like Walmart stating they aim to reallocate employees to customer-focused roles rather than replacing them entirely. Union representatives and technology developers weigh in on the implications of this automation for workers and efficiency in the retail industry.

title: If you invested $1,000 in eBay 10 years ago, here's how much you'd have now
summary: A $1,000 investment in eBay 10 years ago would now be worth over $4,500, representing a 350% return, significantly outperforming the S&P 500 during the same period. The article discusses eBay's evolution from an auction site, its split from PayPal, and its future plans, while also noting PayPal's stronger stock performance since the separation. It concludes with general investment advice about index funds.

title: PD - PagerDuty Announces Second Quarter Fiscal Year 2020 Financial Results
summary: PagerDuty announced strong second quarter fiscal year 2020 financial results, with revenue increasing 45% year-over-year to a record $40.4 million. The company reported over 12,000 customers and highlighted best-in-class gross margins of 85%. PagerDuty also provided financial outlooks for the third quarter and full fiscal year 2020, projecting continued revenue growth and non-GAAP net loss per share.

title: Alibaba has bought a $700m stake in giant music streamer Netease
summary: Alibaba Group has invested approximately $700 million to acquire a minority stake in NetEase Cloud Music, one of China's largest music streaming services. This move strengthens the relationship between the two companies, with NetEase Inc. remaining the majority shareholder. Alibaba also acquired NetEase's e-commerce platform Kaola for $2 billion, integrating it into Tmall while allowing Kaola to operate independently.

title: Apple Inc. v. Pepper: A Case to Watch for Commissions-Based Retailers Selling Directly to Consumers
summary: The U.S. Supreme Court ruled in *Apple Inc. v. Pepper* that consumers could sue Apple for antitrust violations related to its App Store, specifically regarding the 30 percent commission imposed on developers. This decision allows direct purchaser suits against monopolistic retailers using commissions, impacting not just Apple but also other major online marketplaces like eBay, Etsy, Amazon, Jet, Walmart, and Newegg. The article highlights the significant implications for commissions-based retailers selling directly to consumers.

title: Technology firms vie for billions in data-analytics contracts
summary: The article discusses the booming data-analytics market, highlighting companies like C3.ai and Databricks that are vying for billions in contracts. It details the journey of C3.ai's founder, Tom Siebel, and the industry's potential to revolutionize business productivity, despite current challenges in implementing truly sophisticated AI platforms. The piece also notes the significant financial valuations and growth projections for the data analytics sector.

title: We toured an Amazon fulfillment center. Here's what we saw.
summary: The article details a tour of an Amazon fulfillment center, highlighting the extensive use of robots and Amazon's significant presence with over 3,000 employees in its 1-million-square-foot facility. It implies an observation of Amazon's operational scale and technological integration.

title: Amazon Brings Prime Program to Brazil to Outflank Local Rivals
summary: Amazon.com Inc. is launching its Prime membership program in Brazil to gain market share against local competitors like MercadoLibre Inc. and B2W Cia. Digital. The service will offer free unlimited shipping for approximately 500,000 products, two-day shipping in 90 cities, and include entertainment perks like Amazon Music and Prime Video. This expansion marks Brazil as the 19th country to offer Amazon's Prime program, underscoring Amazon's long-term investment strategy in growing e-commerce markets.

title: Integral Ad Science Turns Over Entire Senior Leadership Team
summary: Integral Ad Science (IAS) has seen a near-complete turnover of its senior leadership team since Lisa Utzschneider became CEO in January and Vista Equity Partners acquired the company. Eighteen new executives have been hired, and 15 have left, signaling a strategic shift to scale the company and focus on new areas like OTT/CTV. The new hires are younger, more diverse, and less likely to have advanced degrees compared to their predecessors, reflecting a shift in hiring practices influenced by Vista Equity Partners' playbook.

title: HEINZ Achieves the Impossible With Launch of New HEINZ Tomato Ketchup With a Blend of Veggies
summary: HEINZ has launched a new Tomato Ketchup with a Blend of Veggies, incorporating carrots and butternut squash to offer parents a way to include more vegetables in their children's diets without compromising the classic HEINZ taste. This new product contains 25% added veggies and 25% less sugar than regular HEINZ Tomato Ketchup, making it a healthier option for families. It is available in 20 oz. and 31 oz. squeeze bottles at select retailers and online, supported by a comprehensive marketing campaign.

title: Purpose At Work: Why VF Corp Boycotts Brazilian Leather As Amazon Burns
summary: VF Corporation, which owns brands like Vans and The North Face, has severed ties with Brazilian leather suppliers due to the Amazon fires. This decision aims to avoid contributing to environmental harm and signals to the Brazilian government and industry the importance of environmental action. The article highlights how VF Corp's purpose-driven business strategy sets an example for other companies to operate through the lenses of both purpose and profit.

title: SPS Commerce Acquires Mapadoc For $11.5 Million
summary: SPS Commerce has acquired the Mapadoc EDI division of SWK Technologies for $11.5 million in cash. The acquisition strengthens SPS Commerce's position in cloud-based supply-chain software, giving Mapadoc customers access to SPS's retail trading network and other applications. SWK Technologies plans to use the sale proceeds to accelerate its growth strategies centered on SMB digital transformation.

title: Why Markets Think Trump Tariffs Will Help Apple and Hurt Amazon
summary: This article explores why markets believe tariffs will impact Apple positively and Amazon negatively. It highlights Apple's strong embedded position within the Chinese economy, suggesting that China needs Apple as much, if not more, than Apple needs China, thus incentivizing protection from tariffs. Conversely, Amazon's business model, heavily reliant on Chinese-made goods without a similar indispensable role in China's economy, makes it vulnerable to tariff impacts.

title: HeartFlow Announces FDA Clearance for HeartFlow Planner
summary: HeartFlow Inc. has received FDA clearance for its HeartFlow Planner, a non-invasive, real-time virtual modeling tool designed for coronary artery disease (CAD) intervention. This new interactive tool allows interventional cardiologists to model various treatment strategies and explore clinical scenarios before catheterization lab procedures. The HeartFlow Planner utilizes patient CTA data to create personalized 3-D models and simulate blood flow to help determine optimal treatment courses.

title: Russia’s Largest Social Network Starts Dating App to Rival Tinder
summary: VKontakte, Russia's largest social network, has launched a new dating app called Lovina, which focuses on quick-fire video chats to compete with established dating apps like Tinder. The app aims to provide a more authentic and safer dating experience by using video and artificial intelligence to screen for explicit content, while maintaining user privacy. Lovina will be free to use, generating revenue through in-app purchases for profile promotion and access to expanded features.

title: Target 20 Years of Design for All anniversary collection brings back 20 designers Saturday
summary: Target is celebrating 20 years of designer partnerships by bringing back a collection of nearly 300 popular items from 20 designers, including Missoni and Lilly Pulitzer. The "20th Anniversary Collection" goes on sale Saturday, offering a second chance for shoppers to purchase discounted designer items. Shoppers are advised to prepare for high demand, as previous collaborations have sold out quickly and appeared on eBay at marked-up prices.

title: Keurig Dr Pepper launches new line of coffee makers
summary: Keurig Dr Pepper has launched the K-Duo portfolio, a new line of coffee makers that combine single-serve and drip coffee functionality. These brewers offer convenience and versatility by allowing users to brew a single cup with K-Cup pods or a full carafe of drip coffee. The portfolio includes three models with varying features and price points, catering to different consumer needs and occasions.

title: Kaspi.kz CEO Mikhail LOMTADZE: KASPI.KZ TO HOLD IPO ON THE LONDON STOCK EXCHANGE IN 4TH QUARTER 2019
summary: Kaspi.kz CEO Mikhail Lomtadze announced the company's plans to hold an IPO on the London Stock Exchange in the fourth quarter of 2019. The IPO aims to introduce Kazakhstan's innovative technology company to international investors and support its expansion beyond Kazakhstan, particularly into Azerbaijan and other Central Asian/Caucasus markets. Kaspi.kz, already well-capitalized, views the IPO as a strategic move to boost its development strategy and international recognition, rather than to raise additional capital for its current operations.

title: How Jeff Bezos almost bought Netflix for about $15 million
summary: This article recounts Netflix co-founder Marc Randolph's meeting with Jeff Bezos in 1998 regarding a potential acquisition of Netflix by Amazon for approximately $15 million. During the meeting, Randolph and Bezos bonded over their companies' early launch experiences, while Netflix co-founder Reed Hastings showed impatience, eager to discuss the business proposition. The excerpt highlights the contrasting personalities and priorities during these early discussions.

title: Massive store closures are a strategy, not a sign of a ‘retail apocalypse,’ experts say
summary: Experts suggest that widespread store closures are a strategic repositioning of the retail industry rather than a sign of a "retail apocalypse." David Berliner of BDO views these closures as a "survival of the fittest" scenario, indicating a necessary evolution for retailers. He emphasizes that retail is not dying but adapting to new market realities.

title: Gap Inc. Kicked off NY Fashion Week with Celebration of Inclusion
summary: Gap Inc. celebrated inclusion by kicking off New York Fashion Week with Harlem's Fashion Row, highlighting Black fashion designers and expanding diverse talent recruitment. The event featured discussions with industry leaders and designers of color, emphasizing innovation and the company's commitment to equality. Gap Inc. also signed the "Open to All" pledge, reinforcing its long-standing values of diversity and inclusion, and was ranked among the top ten most diverse companies by Refinitiv's Diversity and Inclusion Index.

title: Canal de Las Estrellas de Televisa ya no será gratis en internet... ¡¿Y las comedias?!
summary: Televisa's Canal de Las Estrellas will no longer be free to stream online starting October 2. Viewers will need to subscribe to either Blim TV or Izzi to access the content. This change is a response to the intense competition in the streaming service market.

title: Blackstone CEO Steve Schwarzman on Bitcoin: “I Was Raised in a World Where Someone Needs to Control Currencies”
summary: Blackstone CEO Steve Schwarzman discusses his views on Bitcoin, artificial intelligence, and investment strategies in an interview with Fortune. He expresses skepticism about cryptocurrencies due to the lack of central control and potential for illicit activities but views blockchain technology favorably for other applications. Schwarzman also highlights AI as a major growth area and discusses the ethical challenges associated with technological advancements.

title: Sally Beauty announces private label credit card
summary: Sally Beauty Holdings announced a new private label credit card program for its Sally Beauty Supply and Beauty Systems Group stores, in partnership with Alliance Data. This initiative aims to enhance its existing loyalty program, which boasts over 15 million members, and is expected to pilot in Q2 fiscal year 2020. The move positions Sally Beauty to compete with rivals like Ulta and Sephora, and also to counter Amazon's recent entry into the professional beauty market.

title: Comcast gives away Xfinity Flex TV device, pounding shares of Roku
summary: Comcast announced it will offer its Xfinity Flex streaming media set-top box for free to internet customers, intensifying competition with Roku Inc. This move caused Roku's stock to tumble nearly 14% as investors reacted to the increased competition from a major player like Comcast, alongside existing rivals Amazon, Apple, and Google. The Xfinity Flex aims to simplify the streaming experience by offering access to various services and free content.

title: Amazon’s order of 100,000 Rivian vans signals the automaker is ‘for real’
summary: Amazon's order of 100,000 electric vans from Rivian, led by a $700-million investment, signals the electric vehicle startup's significant emergence in the automotive industry. This massive pre-production order provides Rivian with a major customer ahead of its consumer vehicle launches and validates its potential as a serious automaker, according to analysts. The custom-built vans will be used for Amazon Prime deliveries, starting in 2021, and will share key components with Rivian's R1T pickup and R1S SUV.

title: Amazon is purchasing 100,000 Rivian electric vans, the largest order of EV delivery vehicles ever
summary: Amazon has placed an order for 100,000 electric delivery vehicles from Rivian Automotive, marking the largest order of EV delivery vehicles to date. This move is part of Amazon's broader plan to transition its fleet to run entirely on renewable energy by 2030, with prototypes expected on the road next year and 10,000 vehicles by late 2022. Despite the massive order, Rivian states it will not impact the production rollout of its R1T pickup and R1S SUV in late 2020.

title: Blockbuster Could Have Bought Netflix for $50 Million, but the CEO Thought It Was a Joke
summary: The article recounts a pivotal 2000 meeting where Netflix co-founders offered to sell their company to Blockbuster for $50 million. Blockbuster CEO John Antioco rejected the offer, dismissing Netflix's business model as unsustainable. This decision ultimately contributed to Blockbuster's demise and Netflix's rise.

title: Netflix Stock Drops After CEO Acknowledges ‘Tough Competition’ Coming From Disney, Apple
summary: Netflix's stock dropped significantly after CEO Reed Hastings acknowledged the upcoming "tough competition" from Disney Plus and Apple TV Plus. Investors were unnerved by his comments, despite Netflix having previously addressed the increased competitive intensity in the streaming sector. An analyst, however, predicted a rebound for Netflix's stock, arguing that new entrants won't necessarily steal existing subscribers.

title: Walmart to Stop E-cigarette Sales in US Stores, Company Memo Says
summary: Walmart announced it will stop selling e-cigarettes and electronic nicotine delivery products in its U.S. stores due to growing regulatory complexity and uncertainty. The decision follows bans on flavored vaping products in several states and federal plans to remove all flavored e-cigarettes from shelves amidst concerns about youth nicotine addiction and vaping-related lung disease. Walmart will exit the category after selling through its current inventory.

title: Avantis U.S. Equity ETF ETF Price, Holdings, & News (NYSEARCA:AVUS)
summary: The Avantis U.S. Equity ETF (AVUS) is an exchange-traded fund that tracks the Russell 3000 index, launched on September 24, 2019, and managed by American Century Investments. It features a diversified portfolio of US equities with a bias towards smaller, more profitable, or value companies. As of January 9, 2026, AVUS was trading at $115.05, with $10.80 billion in assets under management and a net expense ratio of 0.15%.

title: Netflix Stock Breaks Down as Competition Heats Up
summary: Netflix stock fell following increased competition from Apple and Disney, causing CEO Reed Hastings to emphasize the company's core strategy of in-house content. Despite concerns about subscriber misses, an analyst suggests that the broader trend of shifting to streaming will outweigh competitive headwinds. Technically, the stock is showing bearish indicators and could see further decline, with its next earnings report due on October 15, 2019.

title: International Coffee Day 2019: 89 Percent of Americans Get their Cup of Joe from Home
summary: A new survey by Reddi-wip, a Conagra Brands product, reveals that 89% of Americans get their coffee from home, citing convenience, cost, and customization as key reasons. To cater to this trend, Reddi-wip is launching a new Barista line of cream-based products, Nitro Creamer and Sweet Foam, designed to offer a coffeehouse experience at home. The survey also highlights that 79% of Americans prefer coffee with add-ins and many look forward to their morning coffee ritual.

title: Amazon buys cloud startup INLT to help merchants import goods
summary: Amazon.com Inc. has acquired cloud startup INLT for an undisclosed amount to help merchants on its online marketplace more easily import goods into the United States. INLT provides software for sellers to manage costs and customs clearance for cross-border shipments, and Amazon plans to offer this technology to its merchants to simplify international sales processes.

title: EBay CEO steps down amid ongoing operating review
summary: EBay Inc. CEO Devin Wenig is stepping down amidst an ongoing operating review, with CFO Scott Schenkel appointed as interim CEO. Wenig, who took over after the PayPal split in 2015, had been under pressure from activist investors to spin off businesses. Despite efforts to modernize EBay and use AI, the company struggled to keep pace with Amazon's growth.

title: Netflix stock turns negative for 2019, but trader sees another big drop ahead
summary: Netflix stock has turned negative for 2019, with one trader predicting a further significant drop due to a lack of support on the charts until $231. This decline is attributed to increasing streaming competition and a recent decrease in subscriber numbers, leading analysts to advise investors to stay away from the stock for the near future.

title: McDonald’s uses Alexa and Google to help with hiring
summary: McDonald's is implementing a new voice-activated job application system using Amazon's Alexa and Google Assistant to streamline hiring. This initiative, dubbed McDonald’s Apply Thru, allows job seekers to start applications through voice commands and is part of a broader technology push by the company to attract employees in a tight job market. The feature is available in multiple countries and aims to help McDonald's fill constant staffing needs across its 38,000 restaurants worldwide.

title: EBay CEO Devin Wenig, at odds with the board, steps down
summary: EBay Inc. CEO Devin Wenig has stepped down amidst pressure from activist investors seeking to break up the company. Scott Schenkel, EBay's CFO, has been appointed interim CEO as the company searches for a permanent replacement. Wenig's departure follows his failure to significantly grow EBay’s marketplace and clashes with the board over the sale of classifieds businesses.

title: EBay CEO resigns as company considers selling assets
summary: EBay CEO Devin Wenig has resigned from his position as the San Jose-based e-commerce company considers selling some of its assets. An interim leader has been appointed following Wenig's departure.

title: Singapore leads in cloud tech
summary: Singapore is leading the cloud computing adoption in Southeast Asia, driven by its advanced digital infrastructure, government support, and high demand for skilled professionals. Despite its leadership, the country faces challenges with cybersecurity, as many firms struggle to keep pace with rapid cloud expansion and data security threats like those leading to data being sold on the Dark Web. However, organizations are encouraged to leverage cloud technology for competitive advantages rather than using it as a mere digital storage solution.

title: Avantis U.S. Equity ETF
summary: This page provides a comprehensive profile of the Avantis U.S. Equity ETF (AVUS), including its price, dividend and valuation, expense ratio, holdings, performance, and ESG scores. It details the ETF's structure (Active ETF), inception date (September 24, 2019), and asset under management (AUM) of $11,023.0 M, offering a deep dive into its characteristics relative to other ETFs in its category and segment. The article also presents various charts, technical analysis, and comparisons to assist investors and financial advisors in evaluating AVUS.

title: 200-acre Synergy Tech Park development in Saratoga County attracting interest from Amazon, UPS and Costco
summary: A 200-acre Synergy Tech Park development in Saratoga County, New York, is drawing interest from major companies like Amazon, UPS, and Costco. The park, located in Clifton Park, is anchored by a new U-Haul regional storage center and is being developed by Mark Rekucki of M.J. Properties Inc. The project aims to create a significant warehouse park in the region.

title: Five Questions with… Bernd Greifeneder, Founder and CTO at Dynatrace
summary: Bernd Greifeneder, Founder and CTO of Dynatrace, discusses the biggest challenges for his clients, which involve transforming into software businesses and moving towards an Autonomous Cloud with automated operations. He expresses excitement about deterministic AI and its application in complex IT environments, highlighting Dynatrace's successful reinvention from application performance management to software intelligence. Greifeneder also shares his greatest success, Dynatrace's IPO, and a lesson learned from a past failure in market analysis.

title: New CEO at Ebay, Microsoft launches its e-commerce tool and international transit time to be reduced in Brazil. E-commerce news by Nabil.
summary: This article covers major e-commerce news including Devin Wenig stepping down as eBay CEO, Microsoft launching its Dynamics 365 Commerce tool to compete in the e-commerce solutions market, and Brazil's national Correios significantly reducing international transit times. It also highlights Rent the Runway's supply chain issues, JD.com's efforts to speed up deliveries, and advancements in drone delivery by FedEx, Walgreens, and Wing Aviation. Additionally, the article notes the U.S. remaining in the Universal Postal Union and Narvar's partnership with Walgreens for Urban Outfitters' pick-up services.
